user.title: Add a Govee light over Bluetooth
user.description: Lights currently seen by a Home Assistant Bluetooth adapter or proxy. Leave model blank to use the one in the advertised name.

bluetooth_confirm.title: Add {name}
bluetooth_confirm.description: Set up {name} ({address}) as a {model} controlled over Bluetooth?

unknown_model.title: Unknown model {model}
unknown_model.description: {model} is not in this integration's model table, so the colour command format it expects is unknown. Home Assistant will now connect to {name} and read its firmware version, power, brightness and current mode. Nothing is written to the light in this step. If the light is showing a plain colour, that read answers the question.

probe_fallback.title: Colour dialect not yet known
probe_fallback.description:
{model} on firmware {firmware} answered the read-only check, but its current mode is {mode}, which does not reveal the colour dialect. {detail}

Choose how to continue. Retrying after putting the light into a plain colour in the Govee app is the safest option.

active_consent.title: Run the active probe?
active_consent.description:
The active probe writes a test colour to {name} ({model}) in each colour dialect this integration knows, then reads the mode back to see which one the light echoes. For the RGBIC dialect (0x15) the test is a white at a set colour temperature, because that mode's reply carries the temperature but no colour.

Before you continue:

- The light will change colour briefly.
- Writes in an unsupported format have not been seen to damage either tested light (H6159, H6181), but this cannot be guaranteed harmless.
- If the light stops responding, recovery is a power cycle of the light followed by a reload of this integration's config entry.

The probe never sends scene IDs and never writes brightness above 100. Power, brightness and colour are restored afterwards where the light's state allows it.

data.consent: I understand the light will change colour and that writes cannot be guaranteed harmless

active_failed.title: Active probe did not find the dialect
active_failed.description:
The active probe on {model} tried sub-modes {attempted} without a confirmed echo. {detail}

You can finish with the default H6159 dialect and change the colour sub-mode under Configure later. The frames exchanged are in this entry's diagnostics download, which is what to attach to an issue.

progress.probe: Reading the current state of {name}. This can take a little while over a Bluetooth proxy.
progress.active_probe: Writing test colours and a test white to {name} and reading the mode back. The light will change colour briefly.

error.consent_required: Tick the box to run the active probe, or go back to choose another option.

abort.already_configured: This light is already set up.
abort.already_in_progress: Setup for this light is already in progress.
abort.not_connectable: The adapter that saw this light cannot make connections. Add a connectable adapter or an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy with active connections enabled.
abort.no_devices_found: No unconfigured Govee lights are currently visible over Bluetooth.
abort.no_scanners: No Bluetooth adapter or proxy capable of connecting is available.

settings.title: Govee Bluetooth settings
settings.description: Colour sub-mode from the model table: {table_submode}. Detected on the light: {detected_submode}. Brightness scale in use: {effective_scale}.

data.poll_interval: How often to read state from the light
data.idle_disconnect: Keep the Bluetooth connection open after a command for

data_description.poll_interval: Each poll opens a short Bluetooth connection. Lower values give faster state updates but use proxy connection slots more often.
data_description.idle_disconnect: Holding the connection makes consecutive commands much faster. Use 0 to disconnect immediately after every command.
data_description.color_submode: Automatic uses the sub-mode reported by the light, falling back to the model table. Set this only if colour commands are ignored and a probe could not settle it.
data_description.brightness_scale: Automatic derives the scale from the colour dialect (0x02 is 0-255, 0x0D and 0x15 are 0-100). If brightness only ever looks dim or jumps to full, force the other scale.
